messages:
tariq: pulled the monthly least-priv report. spotted ~20 principals with kms.admin role but zero kms activity in 270 days. link: https://redwood-internal/reports/least-priv/4201237890.csv :eyes:

devops-anna: do we have a regex match for historical service-account naming? might help batch identify orphans.

tariq: yep pattern is svc-?acct-kms-.* and svcacct-kms-.*. i filtered by last_seen < now()-270d and role==roles/cloudkms.admin.

```
# sample query (internal)
SELECT principal, project, role, last_seen FROM iam_bindings
WHERE role LIKE '%cloudkms.admin%' AND last_seen < '2023-08-01'
ORDER BY last_seen ASC
LIMIT 50;
```

robert: important: some build infra pick up keys for ephemeral jobs; last_seen can be misleading if those jobs rotate through a bastion project. we should check audit logs across projects for Rewrap/Encrypt/Decrypt in the past 12 months before removing.

sre-kim: agreed. also flag: one principal svcacct-kms-legacy-9 has Decrypt events but they're all from a single IP tied to a CI runner that was retired 6 months ago. needs correlation.

access-sweeper-bot: Note: Created ticket SEC-2409 to track orphan KMS principals. Auto-tags: suspect-orphan, kms-admin. Assigned: @tariq. Deadline: 2024-12-01.

devops-anna: propose triage flow: 1) cross-check cloud KMS audit logs for last 12 months 2) query CI inventory for references to the principal 3) send owner ping (email + slack) 4) if no response -> create infra escalation for key-access freeze 5) canary unbind in staging -> prod prune after 5 days stable.

tariq: +1. adding: capture a full key ACL snapshot (export current IAM bindings and key metadata) and store in compliance ledger. ensures rollback possible.

robert: how will we freeze key-access? KMS doesn't support soft-disable. we could add a deny binding to the principal and rely on 'deny policies' for a short window, then remove the admin binding. need to coordinate with GCP policy team.

sre-kim: alternative: rotate key primary version and revoke the old version from the principal via IAM change. but rotation touches all consumers. prefer deny binding for minimal blast radius.

```
# example deny policy snippet
bindings:
  - role: roles/iam.denypolicy
    members:
      - serviceAccount:svcacct-kms-legacy-9@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

pager-bot: Automated: Security advisory DEF-51 triggered for principal svcacct-kms-legacy-9 (no owner, high-scope KMS role).

devops-anna: who owns the 'owner ping' step? i can draft the standard message. include required evidence: last_seen query, audit-log snippet, config references, and a 72h response window.

tariq: i'll file the owner ping and copy the infra rotation mailing list. template:

```
Hi — we detected an admin grant for {{principal}} with no activity in 9 months. Please provide owner-proof or request extension within 72h. If no response, we'll proceed with staged removal.
```

robert: include contact for immediate rollback if removal breaks something — e.g., 'ping infra-oncall and pagers if any auth regressions'.

sre-kim: add automated smoke tests after each change: token-issuance, session-rotation, backup-key unwrap. if any fail, auto-revert the deny binding. can we script that?

access-sweeper-bot: FR logged: FR-421  Add reversible deny-and-smoke-run playbook for KMS admin removal. Priority: medium.

devops-anna: small security note: collect ownership evidence into the secure ledger only, avoid attaching PII in public threads.

tariq: good catch. will redact user emails in the ticket.

robert: question for sec: do we need to run vuln triage on any configs discovered during the audit (e.g., overly broad key labels or cross-project bindings)? i'd argue yes for any key with project:allBindings or org-level admin.

robert: found one key with org-level binding: projects/org-secrets/keys/credentials has binding roles/cloudkms.admin at org level to group infra-legacy@redwood.org. filing SEC-2411 for triage.

access-sweeper-bot: Created SEC-2411: org-level KMS admin found. Triage assigned to @robert.

devops-anna: timeline for SEC-2409 principals: evidence collection 48h, owner ping 72h, staging canary during next quiet window (2024-11-12 02:00 UTC), prod prune earliest 2024-11-20 after successful smoke tests.

sre-kim: i'll prepare smoke test scripts and a dashboard alert for KMS error rate (Decrypt failures, 5xx) and token issuance error trend.

tariq: lastly, suggestion: add a weekly report to the eng-security channel summarizing suspect-orphan principals with risk score (based on role scope, last_seen, org-level binding). helps prioritize cleanups.

robert: +1. include quick links to remediation playbooks. also add a flag for 'used-by-ci' which lowers priority if true but still requires owner-proof.

devops-anna: ok i'll open FR-422: weekly suspect-orphan digest and include risk scoring.

access-sweeper-bot: Update: SEC-2409 status set to "triage in progress".
